milestones.event: Founded in Boise, Idaho; early focus on 64K DRAM in a former potato-field fab.
Acquires Texas Instruments' memory business, becoming a major DRAM player.
Debuts the Hybrid Memory Cube — stacked memory with through-silicon vias (TSVs), the architectural ancestor of HBM.
Acquires Elpida (Japan), becoming the world's #2 DRAM maker.
Sanjay Mehrotra becomes CEO; sharpens focus on technology leadership and high-value segments.
First high-volume HBM (HBM2E) enters the market.
Announces up to $100B US manufacturing plan, anchored by the Clay, New York megafab.
HBM3E launch for AI accelerators; G9 3D NAND enters volume production — first 9th-generation NAND to ship in an SSD.
First in the industry to sample 1γ (1-gamma) sixth-generation DRAM; exits the Crucial consumer brand to redirect supply to AI data centers.
HBM4 36GB in high-volume production for NVIDIA Vera Rubin; world's first PCIe Gen6 SSD (9650) ramps; 256GB DDR5 server modules sampling.

notes: In December 2025 Micron exited its 29-year-old Crucial consumer brand (shipments ended February 2026; warranties honored) to redirect DRAM and NAND supply to AI data-center customers.
FY2026 revenue was a record $133.2B with DRAM at ~73% of sales; 1γ DRAM and G9 NAND are on track to become the highest-volume nodes in company history.
Next-generation DRAM and NAND nodes are on track for volume production in the second half of calendar 2027.
overview: Micron Technology is an integrated device manufacturer (IDM) that designs, builds and sells memory and storage: DRAM (DDR, LPDDR, GDDR, HBM) and NAND flash (SSDs, managed mobile and embedded storage), plus NOR flash for embedded systems. It is the only company headquartered in the US that manufactures leading-edge memory at scale, competing primarily with Samsung and SK hynix.

Unlike fabless chip companies, Micron owns its fabs and develops its own process technology — currently 1γ (1-gamma) DRAM and G9 3D NAND — and vertically integrates everything down to its own SSD controllers and firmware. Roughly three-quarters of revenue comes from DRAM; the rest is mostly NAND. Four business units serve the markets: Compute & Networking (data center, AI, client), Mobile, Embedded (automotive, industrial) and Storage (SSDs).

items.name: HBM4
items.desc: 36GB 12-high stacks in high-volume production for NVIDIA Vera Rubin (>2.8 TB/s per stack); 48GB 16-high sampling. 2048-bit interface, ~20% better power efficiency than HBM3E.

items.name: HBM3E
items.desc: 12-high stacks shipping for current-generation AI accelerators.

items.name: DDR5 server RDIMM
items.desc: Sampling 256GB modules on 1γ DRAM at up to 9,200 MT/s using 3D stacking (3DS) with TSVs — over 40% faster than mainstream modules.

items.name: SOCAMM2
items.desc: 48GB–256GB low-power, high-capacity modules for Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPU platforms (up to 2TB and 1.2 TB/s per CPU).

items.name: 9650 NVMe SSD
items.desc: World's first PCIe Gen6 data-center SSD (G9 NAND): up to 28 GB/s reads, 2× Gen5 performance at 2× performance-per-watt.

items.name: 9550 / 7600 NVMe SSDs
items.desc: Mainstream PCIe Gen5 data-center SSDs (PRO/MAX endurance tiers).

items.name: 6600 ION SSD
items.desc: 122TB E3.S QLC SSD on G9 NAND for capacity-hungry AI storage; 245TB class planned.

items.name: DDR5 desktop/laptop DIMM
items.desc: Client DRAM up to 6,400+ MT/s for PCs and workstations.

items.name: 2650 client SSD
items.desc: G9-based client OEM SSD — the first SSD to ship with 9th-gen NAND.

items.name: Crucial (discontinued)
items.desc: Consumer DRAM and SSD brand wound down February 2026; Micron now focuses client supply on OEMs and commercial channels.

items.name: LPDDR5X
items.desc: Low-power DRAM for flagship smartphones, up to ~9.6 Gbps data rates.

items.name: UFS 4.0 storage
items.desc: Managed NAND for handsets — faster boot, AI-on-device and camera workloads.

items.name: eMMC
items.desc: Entry-level managed NAND for cost-sensitive phones and IoT.

items.name: Automotive memory
items.desc: Automotive-qualified LPDRAM, UFS and NOR for infotainment, ADAS and instrument clusters (ASIL-B rated).

items.name: Industrial & embedded
items.desc: NOR flash, SLC NAND and LPDRAM for industrial, networking and IoT.

items.name: GDDR7
items.desc: High-bandwidth graphics DRAM for GPUs and AI accelerators (up to ~40 Gbps).

technologies.name: 1γ (1-gamma) DRAM
technologies.desc: Sixth-generation 10nm-class DRAM node — first in the industry to ship (2025). Built with EUV lithography and high-K metal-gate CMOS; >30% denser than 1β, DDR5 speeds to 9,200 MT/s at ~20% lower power. Now Micron's largest production node.

technologies.name: 1α / 1β DRAM
technologies.desc: Prior nodes still in broad production across DDR4/DDR5, LPDDR5X and GDDR6 portfolios.

technologies.name: Next-gen DRAM (1δ)
technologies.desc: Seventh-generation node in development, on track for volume production in the second half of calendar 2027.

technologies.name: GDDR7
technologies.desc: Graphics memory for GPUs, gaming and AI accelerators; data rates up to ~40 Gbps, roughly double GDDR6.

technologies.name: LPDDR5X
technologies.desc: Low-power DRAM for smartphones and thin-and-light PCs, up to ~9.6 Gbps with lower voltage than DDR5.

technologies.name: DDR5
technologies.desc: Mainstream server and client DRAM; Micron's 1γ-based DDR5 reaches 9,200 MT/s for data centers.

technologies.name: G9 3D NAND
technologies.desc: Ninth-generation 3D NAND — first in the industry to ship in an SSD (2024). Fastest NAND I/O in production (3.6 GB/s), ~73% denser than rivals; ships in TLC and QLC flavors across client, data-center, mobile and auto.

technologies.name: G8 3D NAND
technologies.desc: Eighth-generation NAND used in the 9550 and 7600 data-center SSDs; six-plane architecture for high parallelism.

technologies.name: HBM (stacked memory)
technologies.desc: Stacks of ultra-thin DRAM dies joined by thousands of through-silicon vias on a logic base die — terabytes-per-second bandwidth for AI training and inference. HBM4 doubles the bus to 2048 bits vs HBM3E.

technologies.name: Advanced packaging
technologies.desc: 3D die stacking (3DS), TSV interconnect and small-form-factor compression-attach modules (SOCAMM) that put server-class capacity in a low-power footprint.

technologies.name: In-house controllers & firmware
technologies.desc: Micron designs its own SSD controller ASICs, firmware and validation stack around its NAND and DRAM — full vertical integration from media to finished drive.
